mainTopic: Guarantors (עָרֵב and קַבְּלָן): when the lender may go to them, which wording creates each kind, collecting from a borrower's property, and a guarantor who paid an orphans' debt.
overview: This amud finishes the משנה with the view of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: if the borrower has property, the lender cannot collect from any guarantor, not even a קַבְּלָן. רבי יוחנן teaches that we usually follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in the משנה, but the guarantor case is one of three exceptions. רב הונא then explains the wording: 'lend him' makes a regular עָרֵב, and 'give him' makes a קַבְּלָן. The גמרא asks about mixed wording, and רבי יצחק, רב חסדא and רבא each draw the line differently. אמימר says 'give him, and I will give' frees the borrower completely, but the גמרא rejects this unless the guarantor handles the money himself. A story about רב חנין teaches that a lender must demand payment from the borrower before seizing his property, because property works like a guarantor. Finally, a guarantor who paid an orphans' debt without telling them cannot collect from the young orphans now. רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע each give a reason.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: no collecting from any guarantor while the borrower has property
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל rules that if the borrower has property, the lender cannot collect from either a regular עָרֵב or a קַבְּלָן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: If the borrower has property, then for both kinds of guarantor, the lender may not collect from them.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the משנה. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל gives his own view about guarantors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the משנה, the first opinion split the two guarantors. With a regular עָרֵב, the lender must first go to the borrower. With a קַבְּלָן, the lender may go straight to the guarantor. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל removes that difference: as long as the borrower has property, the lender must collect from the borrower and not from either guarantor.

keyTerms.meaning: A regular guarantor. He pays only if the borrower cannot.
A stronger guarantor who accepts the debt as if it were his own.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
If the borrower has property,
whether this one or that one,
phrases.notes: 'This one and that one' means both kinds of guarantor: the regular עָרֵב and the קַבְּלָן.

phrases.english: he may not collect from them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה with a disagreeing opinion about the קַבְּלָן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: While the borrower has property, the lender cannot collect from any guarantor, not even a קַבְּלָן.

steps.title: We follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in the משנה except in three places
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל throughout the משנה, except in three cases. The guarantor case is one of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Wherever רבן שמעון בן גמליאל taught something in our משנה, the הלכה follows him, except for the guarantor, צידן, and the last proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a general rule for deciding the הלכה whenever רבן שמעון בן גמליאל appears in the משנה. It lists three exceptions, and our case of the עָרֵב is the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually his view is the הלכה. Here, though, we do not follow him. So the first opinion in the משנה stands: a lender may go straight to a קַבְּלָן even if the borrower has property. The other two exceptions are cases found in other places in ש״ס.

keyTerms.meaning: The final law follows his opinion.
Our משנה, meaning the collection of the משנה.
The 'last proof', a dispute about bringing evidence late.

steps.whatToRemember: In practice we do NOT follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל about guarantors. A lender may go straight to a קַבְּלָן.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Chana said that Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁשָּׁנָה רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בְּמִשְׁנָתֵנוּ –
phrases.english: Wherever Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel taught in our Mishnah,
the halacha follows him;
except for the guarantor, Tzaidan, and the last proof.
phrases.notes: The 'guarantor' exception is our משנה. 'Tzaidan' is a story in גיטין עד. 'The last proof' is a dispute in סנהדרין לא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the הלכה against the opinion just quoted in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in the משנה except for the guarantor, צידן, and the last proof.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical law: a קַבְּלָן can be pursued first, even when the borrower has assets.

steps.title: רב הונא: phrases starting with 'lend him' make a regular guarantor
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא lists four phrases that begin with 'lend him'. All of them create a regular עַרְבוּת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: 'Lend him and I am a guarantor,' 'Lend him and I will repay,' 'Lend him and I am obligated,' 'Lend him and I will give': all of these are the language of a regular guarantee.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now moves to a new question: what exact words make a person a regular עָרֵב? רב הונא says any phrase that opens with 'lend him' does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even strong-sounding endings like 'I will repay' or 'I am obligated' do not make him a קַבְּלָן. Because he started with 'lend him', the loan is still the borrower's own debt, and the speaker only backs it up.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
'Lend him and I am a guarantor';
'Lend him and I will repay';
'Lend him and I am obligated';
'Lend him and I will give',
all of these are the language of a regular guarantee.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: the wording that creates each kind of guarantor.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any phrase beginning 'lend him' creates a regular עַרְבוּת, no matter how it ends.

steps.title: רב הונא: phrases starting with 'give him' make an unconditional guarantor
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא lists the matching four phrases that begin with 'give him'. All of them create קַבְּלָנוּת.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Give him and I am an unconditional guarantor,' 'Give him and I will repay,' 'Give him and I am obligated,' 'Give him and I will give': all of these are the language of an unconditional guarantee.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא finishes his teaching with the other side of the list. Phrases that begin with 'give him' make the speaker a קַבְּלָן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The endings here are the same as in step 3 ('I will repay', 'I am obligated', 'I will give'). Only the opening word changed, from 'lend' to 'give'. So the opening word decides the status: 'give him' makes him a קַבְּלָן, who can be collected from directly.

keyTerms.meaning: An unconditional guarantee, the status of a קַבְּלָן.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not look at the end of the sentence to decide! 'I will repay' appears in both lists. Only the first word, 'lend' (הַלְוֵהוּ) or 'give' (תֵּן לוֹ), makes the difference.
steps.whatToRemember: 'Lend him' means a regular עָרֵב. 'Give him' means a קַבְּלָן.

phrases.english: 'Give him and I am an unconditional guarantor';
'Give him and I will repay';
'Give him and I am obligated';
'Give him and I will give',
all of these are the language of an unconditional guarantee.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב הונא's statement with the matching list for קַבְּלָנוּת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any phrase beginning 'give him' creates קַבְּלָנוּת, no matter how it ends.
steps.whyThisMatters: Together with step 3, this gives רב הונא's view of when a lender may go straight to the guarantor: when the guarantor said 'give him'. Steps 7 and 8 show that רב חסדא and רבא draw the line differently.

steps.title: What if the wording is mixed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about two mixed phrases. One is 'lend him, and I am a קַבְּלָן.' The other is 'give him, and I am a עָרֵב.'
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: if someone says 'Lend him, and I am a קַבְּלָן,' or 'Give him, and I am a עָרֵב,' what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question about phrases that mix the two lists of רב הונא. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב הונא's lists, 'lend him' made a regular ערבות and 'give him' made קבלנות. Now the opening word points one way and the title the person gives himself points the other way. The question is which part of the sentence decides.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (the חכמים)

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
'Lend him, and I am an unconditional guarantor';
'Give him, and I am a guarantor' — what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the two lists of רב הונא from steps 3 and 4 and asks about phrases that cross between them.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the opening word ('lend' or 'give') decide the kind of guarantee, or does the title (עָרֵב or קַבְּלָן) decide it?

steps.title: רבי יצחק: the guarantor title decides
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק answers that the word עָרֵב or קַבְּלָן decides the case. The 'lend' or 'give' opening does not matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: language of ערבות makes a regular ערבות. Language of קבלנות makes קבלנות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק answers the question by looking at what the person called himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Lend him, and I am a קַבְּלָן' is קבלנות, because he said קַבְּלָן. 'Give him, and I am a עָרֵב' is a regular ערבות, because he said עָרֵב. The title is the clearer statement, so it outweighs the opening word.

keyTerms.meaning: Regular guarantee: the lender goes to the borrower first
Unconditional guarantee: the lender may go straight to the guarantor

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
The language of a guarantee makes a regular guarantee,
phrases.notes: He means whichever title the person used for himself, עָרֵב or קַבְּלָן.

phrases.english: the language of an unconditional guarantee makes an unconditional guarantee.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question in step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The title the person gives himself (עָרֵב or קַבְּלָן) decides. The 'lend' or 'give' opening does not.

steps.title: רב חסדא: almost everything is an unconditional guarantee
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says that every phrase makes קבלנות except 'lend him, and I am a עָרֵב.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: all of them are language of קבלנות, except 'lend him, and I am a עָרֵב.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives a different answer. Only one phrase makes a regular ערבות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב חסדא, a regular ערבות needs both signs pointing the same way: the word 'lend' and the title עָרֵב. If even one sign leans toward קבלנות, it is קבלנות. So both mixed phrases from step 5 are קבלנות.
steps.confusionAlert: רב חסדא's 'all of them' is broader than the mixed cases. It also covers other 'lend him' phrases from רב הונא's first list, so his view differs from רב הונא's split in step 3.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
All of them are language of an unconditional guarantee,
except for 'Lend him, and I am a guarantor.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יצחק and leans heavily toward קבלנות.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Every phrase is קבלנות except 'lend him, and I am a עָרֵב.' Both mixed phrases are קבלנות.

steps.title: רבא: almost everything is a regular guarantee
steps.stepSummary: רבא takes the opposite view. Every phrase makes a regular ערבות except 'give him, and I will give.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: all of them are language of ערבות, except 'give him, and I will give.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a third answer, the mirror image of רב חסדא's. Only one phrase makes קבלנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, קבלנות needs both signs pointing the same way: 'give him' and 'I will give.' Any phrase that leans even slightly toward a regular ערבות is a regular ערבות. So both mixed phrases from step 5 are regular ערבות.

keyTerms.meaning: And I will give (the money back to you)

steps.whatToRemember: There are three views on mixed wording. רבי יצחק says the title (עָרֵב or קַבְּלָן) decides. רב חסדא says everything is קבלנות except 'lend him, and I am a עָרֵב.' רבא says everything is ערבות except 'give him, and I will give.'

phrases.english: Rava said:
All of them are language of a regular guarantee,
except for 'Give him, and I will give.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror image of רב חסדא's view. It leans heavily toward a regular ערבות.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Every phrase is a regular ערבות except 'give him, and I will give.' Both mixed phrases are a regular ערבות.

steps.title: אמימר: "Give him, and I will give" cuts off the borrower completely
steps.stepSummary: מר בר אמימר tells רב אשי that his father held that "give him, and I will give" leaves the מלוה with no claim against the לוה at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר אמימר said to רב אשי: My father said this. If someone says "Give him, and I will give," the lender has no claim at all against the borrower.
steps.whatsHappening: A new opinion is reported about the strongest guarantor phrase, "give him, and I will give." According to אמימר, it moves the whole debt onto the guarantor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps asked whether this phrase makes the guarantor a קבלן, someone the lender may approach first. אמימר goes further: the lender cannot collect from the borrower at all, only from the guarantor. In his view the guarantor fully replaces the borrower.

keyTerms.meaning: "Give him, and I will give": the strongest guarantor phrase

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר בַּר אַמֵּימָר לְרַב אָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: Mar bar Ameimar said to Rav Ashi:
So said my father:
phrases.notes: His father is אמימר, the well-known אמורא.

phrases.english: "Give him, and I will give"
the lender has no claim at all against the borrower.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר בַּר אַמֵּימָר לְרַב אָשֵׁי, הָכִי אָמַר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא said "give him, and I will give" is the one phrase that makes קבלנות. אמימר now makes that phrase even stronger.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying "give him, and I will give" frees the לוה completely. The מלוה may only collect from the guarantor.

steps.title: The borrower is freed only if the guarantor personally hands over the money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects אמימר. The לוה stays obligated unless the guarantor himself takes the money and hands it to the לוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. The borrower is not freed from the lender unless the guarantor himself takes the money and hands it over.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects אמימר's statement. The words "give him, and I will give" are not enough to free the borrower.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The guarantor's promise alone does not wipe out the borrower's debt. Only when the guarantor physically handles the money, taking it from the lender and giving it to the borrower himself, is the deal treated as between the lender and the guarantor. In that case the lender has no claim on the borrower.

keyTerms.meaning: "But it is not so": the גמרא rejecting a statement
Takes and gives by hand: he personally handles the money

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two sides. "Give him, and I will give" can still make the guarantor a קבלן, so the lender may go to him first. What the גמרא rejects is only the idea that the borrower is completely free.

phrases.english: But that is not so;
the borrower is not freed from the lender
unless he takes and gives by hand.
phrases.notes: "He" is the guarantor. He takes the money from the lender and puts it into the borrower's hand himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the statement made in step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that "give him, and I will give" alone frees the לוה completely.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A promise in words does not cancel the borrower's debt. That only happens when the guarantor physically handles the money himself.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The לוה is freed only when the guarantor personally takes and gives the money.

steps.title: A judge lets the lender seize property too early, and רב חנין reverses it
steps.stepSummary: A judge let a מלוה take the לוה's property before anyone demanded payment from the לוה. רב חנין בריה דרב ייבא removed the מלוה from the property.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a judge who let a lender take over the borrower's property before he had demanded payment from the borrower. רב חנין בריה דרב ייבא removed the lender from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about a court case. It is setting up the next step, where רבא explains why the ruling in the story was correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The judge went straight to the borrower's property. He skipped the step of first asking the borrower to pay. רב חנין overturned this, which shows the borrower must be approached before his property can be taken.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally "brought him down": gave him the right to take over the property

phrases.english: There was a certain judge who brought the lender down
into the property [of the borrower]
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording to make clear whose property it was.

phrases.english: before he had demanded payment from the borrower;

phrases.aramaic: סַלְּקֵיהּ רַב חָנִין בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יֵיבָא.
phrases.english: Rav Chanin son of Rav Yeiva removed him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new but related topic: the order in which a lender may collect.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מלוה may not take the לוה's property before first demanding payment from the לוה.

steps.title: רבא praises the ruling: property is like a guarantor, so it cannot be collected from first
steps.stepSummary: רבא praises רב חנין and explains his reasoning. A person's property acts as his ערב, and the משנה, as we understand it, says a lender may not demand payment from the ערב first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Who is wise enough to do this, if not רב חנין בריה דרב ייבא! He holds that a person's property is a guarantor for him. We learned in a משנה: one who lends with a guarantor may not collect from the guarantor. And we have established that this means he may not demand from the guarantor first.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא praises רב חנין's ruling and gives the reason behind it. He brings support from a משנה about guarantors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא compares the borrower's property to a ערב, since both are a backup source of payment. We already know a lender may not go to a ערב before asking the borrower. So he also may not go to the borrower's property before asking the borrower.
steps.whatToRemember: A person's property works like his ערב. Just as a lender must ask the borrower before going to a regular ערב, he must ask the borrower before seizing his property.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a practical court procedure. A lender must first demand payment from the borrower before collecting from his property.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: מַאן חַכִּים לְמֶעְבַּד כִּי הָא מִילְּתָא,
phrases.english: Who is wise enough to do such a thing,

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָאו רַב חָנִין בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יֵיבָא!
phrases.english: if not Rav Chanin son of Rav Yeiva!
He holds:
a person's property
acts as a guarantor for him;
and we learned in a Mishnah:

phrases.aramaic: הַמַּלְוֶה אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ עַל יְדֵי עָרֵב –
phrases.english: One who lends to his fellow with a guarantor
may not collect from the guarantor;
and we have established:
he may not demand payment from the guarantor first.
phrases.notes: So too with property: since it works like a guarantor, the lender must go to the borrower before touching it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מַאן חַכִּים לְמֶעְבַּד כִּי הָא מִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and supports the ruling from step 11.
steps.raayaObject: רב חנין's ruling that a lender may not seize the borrower's property before demanding payment from him.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה "המלוה את חבירו על ידי ערב לא יפרע מן הערב," which we have established means the lender may not demand from the ערב first. This is combined with the idea that a person's property acts as his ערב.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A lender must demand payment from the borrower first. Only after that may he collect from the borrower's property.

steps.title: A guarantor pays an orphans' debt without telling them
steps.stepSummary: A case is brought: a ערב for orphans paid the מלוה before informing the יתומים, and now wants to be repaid by them.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a guarantor for orphans who paid the lender before he told the orphans about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new story about a ערב and young orphans. This line only sets up the case. The next steps tell us how the אמוראים ruled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The borrower died, so the debt now falls on his orphans. The ערב paid the מלוה on his own, without first telling the יתומים, and then turned to them for repayment. Steps 14 and 15 answer whether young orphans must pay him now.

keyTerms.meaning: Orphans (here, young heirs of the borrower)
He paid it (paid off the debt)

phrases.english: There was a certain guarantor for orphans,
phrases.notes: Their father had borrowed with this man as guarantor, and then the father died.

phrases.english: who paid the lender
before informing the orphans.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of ערבות from the earlier steps with a new practical case involving orphans.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A case is presented: a ערב paid the orphans' debt without informing them and seeks repayment from them.

steps.title: רב פפא: young orphans are not obligated in the מצוה of paying debts
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that the young orphans do not repay now, because paying a creditor is a מצוה and minors are not obligated in מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Paying a creditor is a מצוה, and orphans are not people who are obligated to do a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the case. The young orphans do not have to pay the ערב now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא sees paying back a debt as a מצוה. Young orphans are minors, and minors are not obligated in מצוות, so there is nothing to collect from them while they are young. The ערב chose to pay without telling them, so he has to wait.

keyTerms.meaning: Paying a creditor is a מצוה
People who are obligated to perform מצוות

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the debt is cancelled. רב פפא only explains why the young orphans don't pay now, because they are minors.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Repaying a creditor is a מצוה,

phrases.aramaic: וְיַתְמֵי לָאו בְּנֵי מֶיעְבַּד מִצְוָה נִינְהוּ.
phrases.english: and orphans are not obligated to perform a מצוה.
phrases.notes: He means young orphans who are still minors.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: פְּרִיעַת בַּעַל חוֹב מִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the case raised in step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The young orphans do not repay now, since paying a debt is a מצוה and minors are not obligated in מצוות.

steps.title: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע: maybe the father already gave the creditor bundles of money
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע gives a different reason: maybe the father handed the creditor bundles of money, so the young orphans do not pay now.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע said: Say that perhaps he gave him bundles of money.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives another reason why the orphans do not pay the ערב now. He worries that the debt may already have been paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע does not use the מצוה reasoning. He says the father may have given the creditor bundles of money before he died. Young orphans cannot know this or argue it, so we do not take money from them now. Payment waits until they grow up and could find out whether the debt was already paid.

keyTerms.meaning: He handed over to him / gave him to hold

steps.whatToRemember: Both אמוראים agree that the ערב cannot collect from the young orphans now. רב פפא's reason is that paying a debt is a מצוה and minors are not obligated in מצוות. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's reason is that the father may have already paid with bundles of money.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר:
phrases.english: And Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said:
Say that he gave him bundles of money.
phrases.notes: Meaning: maybe the father handed the creditor bundles of coins before he died, so the debt might already be paid.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר: אֵימַר צְרָרֵי אַתְפְּסֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different reason from רב פפא for the same ruling on the case in step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The young orphans do not repay now, because the father may already have given the creditor bundles of money.
